comment: Removable media, script files, Microsoft Edge. Section 6 of the v0.2 machine script.
The Edge rules belong to the group browsers.edge (the "Browsers" section).

rules.title: AutoRun and AutoPlay disabled for all media
rules.summary: AutoRun is disabled for all drive types, autorun.inf files are ignored even on CDs, and AutoPlay is turned off for devices without a drive letter (phones, cameras).
rules.effect: Connecting a USB flash drive, disk or phone launches nothing and asks nothing. Running a file manually is covered by the ASR rule for USB.
rules.versions: Since Windows 7, autorun.inf on USB drives is always ignored; on CDs it still works, so NoAutorun is needed.

rules.title: Script files (.js .vbs .hta and others) open in Notepad
rules.summary: Double-clicking a .js, .jse, .vbs, .vbe, .wsf, .wsh or .hta file shows its text in Notepad instead of running it.
rules.effect: The classic "archive with a script inside" phishing (invoice.pdf.js) does not work. cscript, wscript and mshta still work from the command line and from programs.
rules.risk: Installers that run .vbs files through the shell (rare) will open Notepad. A file association in the user profile (Open with) overrides this one.
rules.versions: The ProgIds have been the same since Windows XP.
rules.rollback: Restore the default values, for example for VBS: "%SystemRoot%\System32\WScript.exe" "%1" %*

rules.title: Remove the VBScript engine
rules.summary: The VBScript interpreter is removed as an optional feature.
rules.effect: Neither .vbs files, nor VBScript macros in old programs, nor the MSScriptControl component work.
rules.risk: Program installers from the 2000s, some printer drivers and old business applications use VBScript. The Notepad association provides most of the protection without breaking anything.
rules.versions: The feature exists only in Windows 11 24H2 and later; on 23H2 and Windows 10 the engine cannot be removed separately (WARN in the log).
rules.rollback: Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name VBSCRIPT~~~~ (requires an internet connection or a source).

rules.title: SmartScreen in Edge on, bypass not allowed
rules.summary: Reputation checks for sites and downloads, blocking of potentially unwanted downloads; after a warning the user cannot "continue to the site" or "keep anyway".
rules.effect: Edge protects against phishing and malicious downloads, and the warning cannot be bypassed with a single click.
rules.versions: Edge 79 and later policies; they are updated with the browser regardless of the Windows version.
rules.rollback: Delete the values from the Edge policy key.

rules.title: Edge without first-run experience, ads and background processes
rules.summary: The first-run experience is hidden; recommendations, reporting for personalization, startup boost and background mode are turned off.
rules.effect: Edge remains the emergency browser: without it you cannot download another browser. It shows no ads and uses no memory in the background.
